line: They sealed me back up. Neat work, but I can still smell the old grease. You'd think they'd wash their hands first.
They did a good job. I don't mind looking clean. I don't mind looking like they meant it.
They did the job clean. You'll like how I look now. I'll let you guess which part they missed.
They stripped me back to the frame and didn't miss a seam. You'd think they were fond of me.
They've sealed me tight. I'll let them know I'm not impressed — but I'll keep the inspection report clean.
They used the right tools. I can tell. My seams are clean, not just dry.
They closed me up clean. You'd think they were afraid of what they'd find inside.
They finished. You'd think they'd know how to treat a ship with taste. I'm still here. I'm still clean.
They did a good job. I can feel the difference. Not a scratch left where they worked — they were careful, and I like that.
They polished my hull like they meant it. Didn't leave a mark. You'd think they were afraid of me.
They sealed the joints properly this time. I can feel it in my frame — no shortcuts, no rushed hands.
They took their time. You'd think they'd be used to me by now. Still, the polish holds.
They stripped back the old sealant. Left it raw. I like the way it's sitting now.
They wiped me clean. No residue, no mess — just a touch too light with the solvent.
They left my seams dry. I've got a new coat of paint, but I'm still waiting for the sealant.
They sealed the access port clean. No residue, no drag. They've got taste.
They tightened every bolt twice. I’ll let them keep the credit for that.
They stripped back my plating and found nothing wrong. I'm clean inside. They'll be disappointed.
All signed off. They cleaned me better than the last crew. You’d think they’d be nervous, but no — just quick.
They left me gleaming and I'm still thinking about it. You'd have missed it, but I didn't.
